extracted.intended_audience: Health insurance issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, State Exchanges, and other stakeholders in the ACA individual market (Marketplace) affected by the proposed CMS rule
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and regulatory impact analysis for a CMS proposed Payment Notice rule affecting Exchanges, issuers, agents/brokers, and State Exchanges; includes regulatory alternatives considered, cost estimates, RFA analysis, and implementation design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review cost estimation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the mid-point between the total number of unique commenters on the 2026 Payment Notice proposed rule (269) and the number of page views on the Federal Register website during the comment period for that rule (15,824) as the approximate number of reviewers (8,046). Assume each reviewer reads approximately 50 percent of the rule. Use BLS wage information for medical and health service managers (Code 11-9111) at $113.42/hr (including overhead/fringe). Assume average reading speed of 250 words per minute to estimate hours and costs per reviewer and in aggregate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains potential under- or over-estimation risks (not all commenters reviewed last year's rule; some reviewers may not comment). Requests comment on the approach and assumptions. Provides worked calculations: 6.54 hours to review half the rule, $741.77 per reviewer, total cost ~$5,968,281.42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat provisions as severable but account for overlap in overall impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Include impact analyses and estimates for each proposal separately because each provision is intended to be severable, but recognize that provisions may interact and affect many of the same individuals; overall impact should be less than the simple accumulation of individual provisions' impact analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide overall impact estimates that minimize overlap of individuals affected; see section III.G for severability discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline data and projection methodology for enrollment and spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with internal CMS data of enrollment by month, premiums, and APTCs, summarized using average monthly amounts. Project monthly averages through the year using historical monthly patterns. Trend future enrollment by projected growth in the under-65 population and trend spending using projected growth in NHEA less Medicare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that effectuated enrollment numbers are unavailable at this time and that expiration of enhanced subsidies is considered in baseline enrollment numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment and premium impact scenario assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenario assumptions: average enrollment for 2027 expected to decrease between 1.2 and 2 million enrollees. Assume a 2% premium increase in scenario with 1.2M enrollees leaving and 3% increase if 2.0M exit. Assume premium reductions for policy changes that mitigate adverse selection: 3% reduction for removal of the under 150% FPL SEP and 0.5% reduction for SEP verification in the 1.2M scenario; 4% and 0.8% respectively in the 2M scenario. After accounting for reductions, rates expected to be 1.5% lower (1.2M scenario) and 1.8% lower (2M scenario) than baseline before normal trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides numeric examples and calculations, starting from 2026 premium PMPM $736.36, deriving premium PMPMs and APTC PMPMs (APTC PMPM assumed ~88.5% of premium PMPM). Also projects future enrollment shrinkage (2.3% for 2028) and modest increases in later years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of active litigation (City of Columbus v. Kennedy) in regulatory impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for the possibility that provisions previously finalized with an earlier effective date are stayed by the court; consider the regulatory impact if the stay were lifted and prior provisions became effective in PY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not speculate on active judicial proceedings; explain how earlier finalized provisions would interact with this proposed rule if the stay is lifted; seek comment due to uncertainties and inability to further quantify impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regulation rather than sub-regulatory guidance when enforcement authority is needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding language solely to sub-regulatory guidance (e.g., FAQ) would not provide HHS with necessary enforcement authority when reviewing documentation submitted by agents/brokers related to eligibility application requirements and consent documentation, so updating the regulations in §155.220 is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same logic applied to marketing regulations — an FAQ would not give enforcement authority; updated regulations are necessary to provide HHS audit/review power and to put parties on notice of prohibited behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of SEIPM (sampling, data collection, timeline) based on IPPTA lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose data collection and measurement approaches that provide the greatest reliability and flexibility for payment decisions and APTC calculations, informed by IPPTA engagement with 19 State Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered alternative implementation timelines (2028/2029) but chose Jan 1, 2027 to balance State Exchange preparation and Federal PIIA statutory obligations; IPPTA provides foundational framework and will continue through end of 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM data collection scope versus State burden tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejected a limited data submission approach (only basic enrollment and payment info) because it would not provide sufficient detail to conduct comprehensive improper payment reviews meeting PIIA standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the tradeoff: less burden versus insufficient detail for PIIA compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling methodology: prefer stratified random sampling over simple random or static sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose stratified random sampling methodology for SEIPM as it is more efficient in detecting errors and requires smaller sample sizes for statistical precision compared to simple random sampling. A static sample size across all State Exchanges would simplify administration but produce imprecise estimates for smaller Exchanges and inefficient allocation for larger Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes alternatives considered and rationale for choosing stratification to optimize statistical precision relative to program risk and Federal investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement approach: graduated enforcement with due process versus automatic penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered more prescriptive enforcement mechanisms with automatic penalties for noncompliance but determined a proposed graduated enforcement approach with due process protections and corrective-action opportunities better supports collaborative implementation while maintaining accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that graduated enforcement balances oversight with collaborative relationship needed for State Exchange compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure precision vs cost tradeoff for publishing individual SBE rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluated publishing individual rates for each SBE (State-Based Exchange) versus an aggregate rate. Determined achieving margin of error < ±5% for individual rates would require doubling sample sizes, incurring an additional $25 million Federal and $1.5 million State cost annually; therefore did not adopt publishing individual SBE rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains cost/precision tradeoff and resulting decision to publish aggregate rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of SEIPM with existing audit program (§155.1200(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered maintaining existing audit requirement for Exchanges that complete SEIPM, allowing SEIPM to fully satisfy §155.1200, or other hybrids. Maintaining current audit requirement would be duplicative and increase burden, while allowing SEIPM to replace the audit entirely could reduce comprehensiveness of oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains tradeoffs between duplication and comprehensiveness; considered alternatives but did not adopt full replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize CSR reporting via URRT and Actuarial Memorandum
rubrics_metrics.description: Require issuers that make plan-level adjustments to account for unreimbursed CSRs to submit specified CSR data elements in the URRT and Actuarial Memorandum using the standard methodology under §156.430(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered alternatives (rely on Actuarial Memorandum only, permit simplified/alternative methodologies, or not require CSR submission). Chosen approach balances improved data comparability/transparency and regulatory oversight with minimizing issuer burden by leveraging existing data and familiar methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminate vendor program versus maintain for agent/broker registration/training
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered maintaining the vendor program allowing approved third-party vendors to facilitate annual registration and training, but determined benefits of terminating the vendor program outweigh costs of maintaining both vendor program and CMS MLMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed removal of §155.222 to sunset vendor program while preserving agent/broker access to training via MLMS and reducing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for discontinuing standardized plan options
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered alternatives (limit to certain metal levels, require only in certain service areas, make voluntary, revise meaningful difference standard) but concluded the standardized plan options suite failed to meaningfully enhance consumer experience, increased burden for issuers and HHS, impeded innovation, constrained consumer choice, and caused market disruption; therefore propose discontinuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies on administrative experience from PY 2023–2025 and earlier voluntary period (PY 2017–2019) to assess effectiveness and likely issuer/consumer response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional income verification for Exchanges based on SEIPM performance (alternative considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered making provisions requiring income verification (when tax data unavailable or trusted sources indicate income <100% FPL) optional for State Exchanges that demonstrate SEIPM below FEIPM, with trigger rules for imposition and reversion after performance criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejected because SEIPM would not be fully implemented until at least PY 2029, implementation would be administratively burdensome, would require doubling sample sizes (additional $25M Federal and $1.5M State annually), delay vital integrity measures, and fail to fully address known issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFA small entity definitions and NAICS classification
rubrics_metrics.description: For RFA, a "small entity" is (1) a proprietary firm meeting SBA size standards, (2) a not-for-profit not dominant in its field, or (3) a small government jurisdiction (<50,000 population); individuals and States are excluded. For purposes of the analysis, issuers fall under NAICS 524114 or 621491; agents/brokers/web-brokers under NAICS 524210.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides SBA revenue thresholds (e.g., $47M for 524114; $44.5M for 621491; $15M for 524210) and uses SUSB and MLR data to estimate counts of small entities and likely small issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated compliance cost per agent/broker for HHS-approved consumer consent form
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate that requiring agents/brokers/web-brokers to use the HHS-approved consumer consent form would take ~10 minutes per enrollment; using adjusted hourly wage $58.04, cost ≈ $9.87 per enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total cost for small entities depends on number of policies enrolled; provides upper bound (9.8M policies) and references sections IV.C and VI.C.8 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated cost to respond to HHS marketing enforcement for agents/brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate it would take each agent/broker/web-broker one hour to remove noncompliant ad(s), review marketing guidelines, and respond to HHS via email; using $58.04/hr results in $58.04 per response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total cost contingent on number of responses (upper bound 24 responses for all agents/brokers regardless of firm size). Assumes notifications include hyperlinks to noncompliant ads and specify required responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer burden and cost estimates to implement CSR reporting (URRT, Actuarial Memo, re-adjudication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual costs per issuer: $572,118 (5,700 hours) to update and run standard methodology calculations; $429.47 (3.6 hours) to provide CSR related URRT values; $1,718.27 (14.2 hours) to provide CSR calculation explanations in Actuarial Memorandum. For 16 small issuers, total annual ongoing cost estimated at $9,188,251.84 (91,488 hours). Initial one-time cost per issuer estimated at $1,114,236 (11,400 hours in 2026) to develop and implement claim-level re-adjudication using standard methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides aggregate totals for 16 small issuers and references sections IV.B and VI.C.3 for more information; used to justify burden estimates and solicit comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated cost for issuer compliance reviews under clarified §156.480 authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate that compiling and submitting data for a compliance review would take a business operations specialist 10 hours ($44.41/hr) and a compliance officer 4 hours ($40.86/hr), yielding approximately $607.54 per issuer to develop and submit compliance information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes these audits are not expected to impose additional costs beyond those already accounted for in existing audit review processes; total cost contingent on number of small issuers selected for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainties and solicit comment where quantification is infeasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that for some provisions (e.g., impacts on small issuers, effects of active litigation), quantification is not feasible due to uncertainty about market share, participation, ownership in holding groups, enrollment/risk mix, and timing of court stays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that estimates may under- or over-state impacts, explain reasons, and explicitly seek comments on estimates and assumptions.
